items.excerpt: As Albany approaches the deadline to approve their city’s budget for next year, some commissioners are advocating for their departments to avoid cuts as the city navigates a $35 million budget gap. items.headline: Troy launches digital gift card for shopping downtown businesses
items.excerpt: Just in time for the holiday season, shoppers have a new way to spend at downtown Troy businesses. The Downtown Troy Business Improvement District (BID) has launched a digital gift card, called the Troy Card, for shoppers to spend at stores, restaurants and other local spots.

items.headline: One in critical condition after serious crash in Canajoharie
items.excerpt: One person is in critical condition after a serious crash in Montgomery County on Wednesday evening. The incident happened on I-90 eastbound near Exit 29 in Canajoharie, according to New York State Police.

items.headline: Homegrown bakery rising to the occasion with new South Glens Falls storefront
items.excerpt: A local mom has expanded her passion of baking from hobby, to micro-bakery, and most recently, a new storefront in South Glens Falls. Whiskey Ridge Sourdough is now open at 63 Main Street.

items.headline: Hochul unveils 5-gigawatt nuclear master plan for New York
items.excerpt: Governor Kathy Hochul unveiled a 30-point master plan on Wednesday to expand New York's nuclear capacity by 5 gigawatts to address rising electricity demand, despite opposition from protesters concerned about potential cost increases and radioactive waste management.

items.headline: How do lithium-ion batteries catch fire?
items.excerpt: After two lithium-ion battery fires happened in Albany County in just the last few days, officials have been sounding the alarm. But how do these lithium-ion batteries catch fire in the first place?

items.headline: Congregation Beth Israel in Schenectady closing
items.excerpt: Congregation Beth Israel is closing, but instead of mourning this moment, temple secretary James Strosberg said they've accomplished their mission.

items.headline: Berkshire Scenic Railway Museum hit by vandalism 3 times in about a week
items.excerpt: The Berkshire Scenic Railway Museum is asking for the public’s help after the trains at their Lenox Rail Yard were vandalized three separate times in about a week on November 9, 14, and 16.

items.headline: Hochul mulls ban on Red Dye No. 3, potassium bromate, and propylparaben
items.excerpt: Governor Kathy Hochul is considering the Food Safety and Chemical Disclosure Act, a bill that would ban three food additives and require companies to publicly disclose safety reports for ingredients approved via the federal GRAS loophole.
